questions.question: Which smallest number to be subtracted from 300, so that the resulting number is completely divisible by 9?
questions.solution:
As per divisibility rule of 9, for any number is divisible by 9 if and only if sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

Then according to divisibility test of 9 and checking from options,

⇒ (300 - 5) = 295

(2 + 9 + 5)/9 = 16/9

⇒ (300 - 6) = 294

(2 + 9 + 4)/9 = 15/9

⇒ (300 - 3) = 297

(2 + 9 + 7)/9 = 18/9 = 2

⇒ (300 - 1) = 299

(2 + 9 + 9)/9 = 20/9

From above calculations,

∴ If 3 number is subtracted from 300 then resulting number is completely divided by 9.

questions.question: What is the value of 13 + 14 +…….+ 20?
questions.solution:
For Arithmetic Progression,

If Sum of terms = Sₙ and first term of progression = a, common difference = d and n = number of terms -

 ⇒ {{}}{S_n} = (n)/(2)( {2a + (n - 1} )d)

Above question is of arithmetic progression,

a = 13, d = 1

⇒ aₙ = a + (n - 1)d

⇒ 20 = 13 + (n - 1)1

⇒ n = 8

⇒ S₈ = (8/2) × [(2 × 13) + (8 - 1) × 1]

⇒ S₈ = 4 × (26 + 7)

questions.question: What is the value of 8(1)/(7) + 5(3)/(7) + 4(2)/(7) + 3(1)/(7)?
questions.solution:
Follow BODMAS rule to solve this question, as per the order given below,

**Step-1:** Parts of an equation enclosed in 'Brackets' must be solved first, and in the bracket,

**Step-2: **Any mathematical 'Of' or 'Exponent' must be solved next,

**Step-3:** Next, the parts of the equation that contain 'Division' and 'Multiplication' are calculated,

**Step-4: **Last but not least, the parts of the equation that contain 'Addition' and 'Subtraction' should be calculated.

Given expression is,

 Rightarrow {{ }}8(1)/(7) + 5(3)/(7) + 4(2)/(7) + 3(1)/(7) = ?

⇒ (57/7) + (38/7) + (30/7) + (22/7) = ?

⇒ ? = (57 + 38 + 30 + 22)/7

⇒ ? = 147/7

⇒ ? = 21

questions.question: A number when divided by 18 leaves remainder 15. What is the remainder when the same number is divided by 6?
questions.solution:
Let the number be n.

Given,

A number when divided by 18 leaves remainder 15-

Let the quotient be a.

⇒ n = 18a + 15

⇒ n = 6(3a) + 15

⇒ n = (6 × 3)a + 6 + 9

⇒ n = 6(3a + 1) + 9

⇒ n = 6(3a + 1) + 6 + 3

⇒ n = 6[(3a + 1) + 1] + 3

⇒ n = 6(3a + 2) + 3

∴Then the reminder is 3 when same number is divisible by 6.

questions.question: If 123457Y is completely divisible by 8, then what will be the digit in place of Y?
questions.solution:
Given,

123457Y is completely divisible by 8.

As per divisibility rule of 8, the number is divisible by 8, if number formed by the last three digits of given number is divisible by 8 or if last three digits are zeros.

Then,

Given number is 123457Y.

Last three digits, 57Y/8

Checking from options,

⇒ 574 : 574/8 = 71.75

⇒ 575 : 575/8 = 71.875

⇒ 578 : 578/8 = 72.25

⇒ 576 : 576/8 = 72

∴ From above calculation if Y is 6 then number 123457Y is completely divisible by 8.

questions.question: P can do a piece of work in 36 days. If Q is 50% more efﬁcient than P, then in how many days can Q do the same work?
questions.solution:
Given,

P can do a piece of work in 36 days.

Q is 50% more efﬁcient than P then,

Ratios of time taken by P and Q is =

⇒ 150 / 100 = 3 / 2

Let Q alone can do same work in a days.

⇒ 3 / 2 = 36 / a

⇒ a = (36 × 2) / 3

⇒ a = 24

∴ In 24 days Q can do same work.

questions.question: P is twice as good as Q and together they ﬁnish a piece of work in 36 days. The number of days taken by P alone to ﬁnish the work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Q's efficiency be 1 unit/day. Since P is twice as efficient, P's efficiency = 2 units/day.

Combined efficiency of P and Q = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day.

Total Work = Combined efficiency × Number of days together = 3 × 36 = 108 units.

Time taken by P alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of P = 108 ÷ 2 = 54 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 54 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ P is twice as efficient as Q.

⇒ P and Q together finish the piece of work in 36 days.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of Q = 1 unit/day.

⇒ Since P is twice as good as Q, efficiency of P = 2 units/day.

⇒ Total efficiency of P and Q working together = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Time taken = 3 × 36 = 108 units.

⇒ Time taken by P alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of P.

⇒ Time taken by P alone = 108 ÷ 2 = 54 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 54 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency & Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If a person is twice as efficient as another, they will take half the time to finish the same piece of work.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. If people work for the exact same number of days, wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their daily efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

This topic works on the exact identical mathematical concept as Time & Work. The only difference applies to emptying or leakage pipes, where the efficiency is considered strictly negative.

questions.question: If the diagonal of a square is 10 cm, then what is the area (in cm²) of the square?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The diagonal of a square is 10 cm.

**Formula used:**

Area of square = (side)²

The perimeter of the square = 4 × side

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/501173f78d456316152593495c96a6737f546a159bf92d9f688a2bd4bc50711b.png] 

The diagonal of a square is 10 cm.

The diagonal of a square = √2 × side of a square

Side of a square = 10 / √2 cm.

Area of a square = side²

Area of a square = (10/√2)²

Area of a square = 100/2 = 50

**∴ Area of a square is 50cm².**

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 750 and a customer pays Rs. 600 for it. What is the discount percentage?
questions.solution:
Given,

The marked price of an article is Rs. 750 and a customer pays Rs. 600 for it.

Let the discount percentage be a%.

Given,

⇒ 750 - 750 × (a/100) = 600

⇒ 750 - 15a/2 = 600

⇒ 1500 - 15a = 1200

⇒ 15a = 300

⇒ a = 300/15

⇒ a = 20

∴ The discount percentage is 20%.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 50% more than its cost price. If a discount of 10% is given, then what is the proﬁt percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price of the article be Rs. 100.

Given,

The marked price of the article is 50% more than its cost price.

The market price of the article =

= 100 + 100 × (50/100)

= 100 + 50

= 150

The market price of the article = Rs. 150

Given,

Discount percentage = 10%

Selling price = 150 - 150 × (10/100)

Selling price of an article = 150 - 15 = Rs. 135

Profit percentage of an article =

= [(S.P - C.P) / C.P] × 100

= [(135 - 100)/100] × 100

= 35%

∴ Profit percentage of an article is 35%.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio of 3 : 4. If 8 be subtracted from each, then the new ratio becomes 17 : 24. What are the two numbers?
questions.solution:
Let the two number be a and b respectively.

Given,

Two numbers are in the ratio of 3 : 4

⇒ a : b = 3 : 4

⇒ a/b = 3/ 4

⇒ a = 3b/4

Given,

If 8 be subtracted from each, then the new ratio becomes 17 : 24.

⇒ (a - 8) : (b - 8) = 17 : 24

⇒ (a - 8)/(b - 8) = 17/24

⇒ (3b/4 - 8)/(b - 8) = 17/24

⇒ (3b - 32)/4(b - 8) = 17/24

⇒ (3b - 32) × 6 = 17 × (b - 8)

⇒ 18b - 192 = 17b - 136

⇒ b = 192 - 136

⇒ b = 56

⇒ a = (3 × 56)/4

⇒ a = 42

∴ The two numbers are 42 and 56 respectively.

questions.question: If the ratio of the cost price and selling price of an article is 5 : 6, then what will be the proﬁt percentage?
questions.solution:
Given,

If the ratio of the cost price and selling price of an article is 5 : 6,

C.P : S.P = 5 : 6

C.P / S.P = 5/6

S.P / C.P = 6/5

Profit percentage =

= [(S.P - C.P) / C.P] × 100

= [(S.P/C.P) - 1] × 100

= [(6/5) - 1] × 100

= (1/5) × 100

= 20

∴ The profit percentage is 20%.

When 80 is subtracted from 20% of the number, the result is 30.

questions.question: A number is ﬁrst decreased by 30% and then increased by 30%. If the number so obtained is 72 less than the original number, then what is the value of the original number?
questions.solution:
Let the original number be n.

Given,

A number is ﬁrst decreased by 30% -

= n - n × (30/100)

= n - 3n/10

= 7n/10

The new number = 7n/10

And then increased by 30% -

= 7n/10 + (7n/10) × 30/100

= 7n/10 + 21n/100

= 91n/100

The number becomes = 91n/100

Given,

⇒ n - 91n/100 = 72

⇒ 9n/100 = 72

⇒ 9n = 7200

⇒ n = 800

**∴ The value of original number is 800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f72be33799c08d3322a2907949d25e7543e352bc7880a277f6efed7f62d7c04b.png] 

We can use the successive percentage method

Total percentage change = [a + b + ab/100]%

Here a = –30 and b = 30, negative sign shows the percentage decrease

Percentage change = –30 + 30 – (30 × 30)/100 = –9

The number will decrease by 9%

9% of the original number = 72

⇒ (9/100) × Original Number = 72

⇒ Original Number = 72 × 100/9 = 800

**∴ The value of the original number is 800**

questions.question: Speeds of a boat along the current and against the current are 16 km/hr and 12 km/hr respectively. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the current?
questions.solution:
**Given,**

Speed downstream = 16km/hr

Speed upstream = 12km/hr

**Formula used:**

Speed of the current = ½ × (speed downstream - speed upstream)

**Calculation:**

Speed of the current = ½ × (16 - 12) = 4/2 = 2

**∴ Speed of the current is 2km/hr.**

questions.question: A person goes from point L to N and comes back. His average speed for the whole journey is 100 km/hr. If his speed while coming back from N to L is 65 km/hr, then what will be the speed of the person (in km/hr) while going from L to N?
questions.solution:
Given,

Speed of person from point N to L = 65km/hr

Let Speed of person from point L to N be a km/hr.

Average speed for the whole journey = 100 km/hr.

If distance of whole journey is same then average speed of journey is =

⇒ 100 = (2 × a × 65)/(65 + a)

⇒ 6500 + 100a = 130a

⇒ 6500 = 30a

⇒ a = 6500/30

⇒ a = 216.67

∴ Speed of person from point L to N is 216.67 km/hr.

questions.question: An amount invested at simple interest gives Rs. 2550 interest at rate of 17% per annum in 3 years. What is the principal (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Let P = principle, N = time and R = rate percent per annum

Then,

Simple interest = (P × N × R)/100

Given,

Simple interest = Rs.2550, R = 17% and N = 3

⇒ 2550 = (P × 17 × 3)/100

⇒ 2550 × 100 = 51 × P

⇒ P = (2550 × 100) / 51

⇒ P = 5000

∴ The principle amount is Rs.5000.

questions.question: The sales of company A in November is how much percent more than the sales of company B in November?
questions.solution:
Given,

Sales of company A in November = 105 crores

Sales of company B in November = 100 crores

Let sales of company A in November be m% more than sales of company B in November.

Sales of company A = sales of company B + sales of company B × (m/100)

⇒ 105 = 100 + 100 × (m/100)

⇒ 105 = 100 + m

⇒ m = 105 - 100

⇒ m = 5

∴ The sales of company A in November be 5% more than sales of company B in November
